rules.text: A confidentiality agreement states its direction, defines Confidential Information, sets the receiving party's obligations, carries the four standard carve-outs, names the permitted disclosures, the term, return or destruction, the remedies, and the governing law and courts.

Every item of the review checklist gets exactly one verdict: Finding, Acceptable, Not applicable or Missing information; each Finding says whether it is a legal issue or a commercial preference, and the two are kept apart.
rules.source: dpa-review SKILL.md, Operating rules (coverage ledger; separate legal defects from commercial preferences)

rules.text: Every finding quotes the supplied paper word for word.
rules.source: dpa-review SKILL.md, Operating rules (quote and anchor findings to the supplied paper)

rules.text: The review is written for one party's side, asked for when it is not clear, and reads each item's general and side-specific points.

rules.text: Proposed edits go into a copy of the supplied Word file as visible tracked changes, never a rebuilt document; nothing outside the edits changes.
